name: Kava
short: Case reports describe rare but serious liver damage, plus skin and neurological reactions. Trial adverse events were mostly mild; a possible interaction with benzodiazepines has been reported.
text: A systematic review of kava safety found that adverse events in clinical trials and short-term surveillance studies were in general rare, mild and reversible, but that published case reports indicate serious adverse events are possible, including dermatological reactions, neurological complications and, of greatest concern, liver damage. A critical analysis of 19 suspected cases in Germany judged a causal relationship very probable in one patient and possible in another, and advised physicians and patients to watch for liver side effects and to stop kava at the first suspicion. In a later systematic review of randomised trials, adverse events were the same as with placebo, although the authors cautioned that liver toxicity is especially possible if kava is taken for longer than 8 weeks. Controlled trials suggested kava does not potentiate the effects of central nervous system depressants, but a possible interaction with benzodiazepines has been reported.
